Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- Track Arsonist douses with set_status key 'doused' value true. An ignite uses up every douse: clear 'doused' on everyone it hit, survivors included (rules: Arsonist). Don't tell anyone they were doused: code tells the doused players who should know.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Executioner revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them. Code also turns an Executioner whose target died tonight into a Jester at dawn: don't set any status for it.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Code tells the Scout their result every night from your record_visits list; don't tell() them anything about it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- Armed (a trait, R24): a player whose trait_actions has trait 'Armed' fires their one hidden-gun shot at its target, in addition to their role's action. It is an action and a visit (R6; record it, and an alerting Veteran's attack hits the shooter): a role-block stops it along with their role's action, and then the shot isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the fire_gun op (it marks the shot used, even if the attack fails) and resolve a Basic Attack on the target (R3): a kill's cause is 'a hidden gun' and its by is the shooter. Tell the shooter only whether their shot killed its target, never the target's role, and tell a surviving target they were attacked.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Bob as Enforcer; Carol as Prosecutor. Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- Track Arsonist douses with set_status key 'doused' value true. An ignite uses up every douse: clear 'doused' on everyone it hit, survivors included (rules: Arsonist). Don't tell anyone they were doused: code tells the doused players who should know.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Executioner revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them. Code also turns an Executioner whose target died tonight into a Jester at dawn: don't set any status for it.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Code tells the Scout their result every night from your record_visits list; don't tell() them anything about it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- Armed (a trait, R24): a player whose trait_actions has trait 'Armed' fires their one hidden-gun shot at its target, in addition to their role's action. It is an action and a visit (R6; record it, and an alerting Veteran's attack hits the shooter): a role-block stops it along with their role's action, and then the shot isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the fire_gun op (it marks the shot used, even if the attack fails) and resolve a Basic Attack on the target (R3): a kill's cause is 'a hidden gun' and its by is the shooter. Tell the shooter only whether their shot killed its target, never the target's role, and tell a surviving target they were attacked.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Bob as Enforcer; Carol as Prosecutor. Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- Track Arsonist douses with set_status key 'doused' value true. An ignite uses up every douse: clear 'doused' on everyone it hit, survivors included (rules: Arsonist). Don't tell anyone they were doused: code tells the doused players who should know.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Executioner revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them. Code also turns an Executioner whose target died tonight into a Jester at dawn: don't set any status for it.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Code tells the Scout their result every night from your record_visits list; don't tell() them anything about it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- Armed (a trait, R24): a player whose trait_actions has trait 'Armed' fires their one hidden-gun shot at its target, in addition to their role's action. It is an action and a visit (R6; record it, and an alerting Veteran's attack hits the shooter): a role-block stops it along with their role's action, and then the shot isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the fire_gun op (it marks the shot used, even if the attack fails) and resolve a Basic Attack on the target (R3): a kill's cause is 'a hidden gun' and its by is the shooter. Tell the shooter only whether their shot killed its target, never the target's role, and tell a surviving target they were attacked.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Bob as Enforcer; Carol as Prosecutor. The Archivist has a related gap: it is also an exact-role check, but nothing says plainly that a Disguised player's fake role can show up in the archive as one of the "real" entries. Either the rules or the code is wrong. Minor: Frank's Day 4 claim in the ledger reads 'D2: Innocent on Mallory? no: Guilty on Mallory', which is a garbled self-correction kept word for word. Everything else matched the rules as far as I could check: my N3 Good 2 of Carol, Grace and Heidi is correct, the Katana stopped by the trap with a hitback that Grace survived through self-Diviner Strong Defense is correct, and the heartbreak chain is correct.

Let players auto-append the night's pending result to their will even if they die (or explicitly say it is lost, as now, but more visibly). Add an optional per-night claimed-visits table to the public ledger, since Fortune Teller and Cartographer counts drive a lot of the play. Remove free-form self-corrections from claim summaries.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) Chronicler vs Disguised: this was the biggest conflict, and it may have decided the game. The Chronicler text says a marked player's death "reveals their true role ... (an exact-role check, R19)". But R19 and Disguised say every exact-role check sees the disguise, "alive or dead". Bob was a Talent Agent disguised as Enforcer, and Carol had marked him. When he was hanged on Day 3, the reveal said "Talent Agent". Earlier, on Night 1, Heidi's Archivist list had shown his disguise (Enforcer). So two exact-role checks on the same player gave different answers. Under R19, the reveal should probably have said Enforcer. Bob's whole plan rested on that ("my disguise means exact-role checks see me as Enforcer"), and the town used the reveal to confirm Olivia's census.
2) Heartbreak: Bonded says heartbreak "isn't an attack". But Carol's death notice said "You were attacked tonight (heartbreak) and died." Either the rule or the wording is wrong.
3) Diviner on yourself: Grace picked herself on Night 3 to get Strong Defense against a trap hitback. The rules allow self-targets by default, and R6 makes that a self-visit, so I let it stand. But the Diviner text ("skipping yourself" in the group) doesn't say whether this is intended. It also adds Grace as a visited player in the Fortune Teller count (3 visited), which players can't easily reason about.
4) Whether a trap carries over: Dave took "no action" on Night 3 while his Night 2 trap was still on Olivia. I ruled that the trap stays and is armed. The rules support this, but a log line saying "no action" next to "your trap went off" looks inconsistent.
answers.missing_information: I kept track of these by hand: the seat circle after deaths (for Diviner/Surveyor groups), visit graphs for the Fortune Teller, Scout and Cartographer, which nights each trap was armed, each disguise and whether a given check should see it, who has which traits (Bonded pairs, Zealot, Selfish), and token counts. A per-night state table would have helped: holder, armed traps, defenses, visits after swaps, and pending revenges (the Executioner revenge on the night after Judy left).
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a way to check, before a Chronicler reveal went out, whether the result should go through the Disguised lookup. I also wanted to be able to flag the Bob reveal as possibly wrong while the game was still running.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
- The Chronicler reveal ignored Bob's disguise ("Talent Agent" instead of Enforcer), while Heidi's Archivist result used it. That breaks R19.
- Heartbreak was reported as an attack.
- Frank's Day 4 claim ledger has a garbled line ("D2: Innocent on Mallory? no: Guilty on Mallory"). The player wrote that, so it isn't a moderator error, but the claim tool accepted it as written.
Everything else I checked was consistent: Night 1 had 7 visitors and 4 visited (Mallory's sleepwalk to Grace explains the extra visited player), Night 2 had 6 and 5, Night 3 had 4 and 3 (Grace's self-visit is the third visited player). The census, Seer and Diviner groups were all right. Grace's Strong Defense beat the Strong hitback, so she survived, and the trap stopped the Katana but ignored the Divine/Astral revenge. Judy's Grudge didn't fire because she left rather than being hanged. The final win list is correct, including Niaj as Selfish and alive.
answers.suggestions:
- Settle the Chronicler wording: either it shows the disguise like every other exact-role check, or Disguised lists it as an exception. Then have the program apply that one rule everywhere.
- Change the heartbreak notice to "You died of heartbreak", not "attacked".
- Spell out what a Diviner self-target does (whether it's allowed and whether it counts as a visit).
- Give the moderator automatic visit-graph and count tools, a trap/defense state panel, and a trait lookup when a result goes out.
- Check claim-ledger entries for contradictions.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: If your trap goes off but nobody dies of the Strong hitback, the attacker probably had Strong Defense. A Yakuza Diviner who targets themself gets exactly that, and Narrow Escape also does it. Post this right away and look at whoever claims a visit to the trapped player. Don't treat it as a dead end.

Explaining a Day 2 visit as 'a protective action not active until N2' tells the Yakuza you are a Trapper. They will then plan around the hitback with self-defense or an Astral attack. If you have to explain a visit, give the target but not the mechanism, or have a cover ready.

Visit-count math (Fortune Teller, Cartographer) is wider than it looks. The Katana holder can use their own role's action AND make the Katana visit, so one claimed visitor can cover two visits. Use the counts only to rule out claimed non-visitors, never to pin one claimant.

An unclaimed player who keeps pushing one specific target, and threatens to nominate before there's any data, fits an Executioner. Executioner revenge hits a random Guilty voter, and Bonded pairs can then die of heartbreak. When the hang is clear anyway, keep the Guilty count near a bare majority so fewer key info roles are exposed.

A claimed Tracker whose tracks always land on players with passive or no-visit roles is giving results nobody can check. That fits a Neutral killer (Arsonist/Serial Killer), who reads Not Evil and is invisible to a census. Test them with a watch or a hang near the endgame.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death and list quiet unclaimed players and unexplained survivors (a Not Evil read doesn't clear them).
tips_feedback.why: Frank was an Arsonist whose fake Tracker results could never be checked. Once Grace died and the game didn't end, hanging him at final 4 won it for the Village.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid hinting at a power role early or announcing tonight's target
tips_feedback.why: My Day 2 'protective action not active until N2' gave away Trapper. The Yakuza then had Grace self-Divine for Strong Defense before attacking Olivia, so my trap's hitback didn't kill.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claimant is often real: test both before hanging or shooting either.
tips_feedback.why: Here both Tracker claimants (Frank and Grace) were fake, one a Neutral and one Yakuza. Duplicate claims of a convenient no-token info role can be two covers.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it, so post what matters publicly.
tips_feedback.why: Olivia's and Carol's wills and the Chronicler reveal of Bob showed the census and marks were real. That narrowed the Yakuza and Neutrals in the endgame.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows someone Yakuza, suspect whoever argued to delay their hang, defended them or PM'd them
tips_feedback.why: Alice reasoned that Grace was the only non-Yakuza Guilty vote alongside Bob/Mallory on Frank, then sniped her. Grace was the last Yakuza.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: lessons on trap hitback failures, role hinting, visit-count math, Executioner reads and Neutral fake trackers.

lessons.tip: Put your mark on the player most likely to be hanged next. A marked hang shows the true role publicly, so the vote either confirms a Yakuza or clears the suspect's accuser. But afterwards every Guilty voter is at risk of a Divine revenge. If you're Bonded, your partner's death kills you too, so keep the Guilty votes near a bare majority when the hang is already safe.

lessons.tip: Push your target in the town's own words: demand a plain claim, set a deadline ('if it's still missing on my next turn, I'll nominate'), and vote with the majority on everyone else. When your target holds back info, you look like a diligent villager, not a Neutral.

A hang that a quiet or late-claiming player pushed hard can be an Executioner's win. The revenge Divine Attack then lands on a random Guilty voter. If an Evil read is solid, keep Guilty votes near a bare majority so fewer villagers are exposed to Executioner or Jester revenge.

Killing an investigator doesn't stop their result if their will names tonight's target. Ivan's will named a Bob+Carol pair, and that alone condemned Bob. Kill the investigator the night before they commit to a target, or make sure the teammate in that check has an airtight cover.

lessons.tip: Douse players likely to live, not the obvious Katana target. A douse on someone who dies to another cause is wasted. Day 1's agenda-setter or a freshly claimed investigator often dies that night, so douse quiet or confirmed-looking townies the Yakuza will leave alone.

Once you've survived a trial, ignite the next night, even with only 1-2 players doused. Each extra night of dousing gives a Fortune Teller or Cartographer another count with an unexplained visitor in it. Killing the player who is tracking the counts removes your biggest threat.

lessons.tip: A Tracker cover whose every result is 'visited nobody' on passive-role players gets called uncheckable and wasted. Pick tracks that could be checked but probably won't be, or claim a role whose visits match your real douse targets. Then visit counts and Lookouts back up your story instead of leaving an unexplained extra visit.

At 4-5 alive, a 'Yakuza cleared' census or a Village-only trait (Armed, a Sniper shot) makes that player near-confirmed. If you attack them, the others will side with them. Get yourself out of the top suspect spot before the final few. Kill the counter or claimer before you're the only one left unexplained.

An alignment census counts only Good or Evil, never Neutral. So 'Evil 0' clears a player of Yakuza but not of being a Neutral killer. Use the census's Good count, or other checks, to rule out Neutrals.

lessons.tip: After any trial, match each player's stated vote against the announced totals and keep the list. Once a player flips Yakuza, any non-Yakuza who sat in a small Guilty or Innocent minority with them is a strong teammate lead. Count claimed Zealot or Merciful votes when you do this.

Claim and shoot on the same turn once you have a mechanical lead near the endgame. A shot that kills a Yakuza effectively confirms you, and your vote then steers the final hang. Don't save the shot past the point where the Yakuza could reach the vote lock.

When checking a Fortune Teller's visit counts, remember that the Katana holder can use their own role's action and also make the Katana visit. A gap of one in the visited count usually means a holder who visited two players, so look at whoever is the lone claimed visitor to the night's attack target.

An Archivist list gains credibility when roles on it are claimed later by players who couldn't have known. A role on the list that a suspect borrows after the list is posted (here Enforcer) should be treated as likely fake until it is checked.

An Archivist or role list that names roles before anyone has claimed them is strong evidence the list is real. A claim that matches the list but appears only after it was posted, especially after a holdout, is the weakest kind of claim. Test it, or hang that player if a census or Chronicler mark can settle it.

Spend Chronicler marks on the suspect in a live two-way split (for example a census that says 'one of Bob or Judy is Evil'). Hanging the marked suspect then reveals their role and resolves the split in public, whichever way it falls.

tips_feedback.why: I never claimed, but setting the Day 1 agenda was enough for the Yakuza to read me as an investigator and kill me N1. The tip's warning applies to leadership behaviour too, not just hints.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's Seer pair and Olivia's census, posted at the right moments, got Mallory and Bob (both Yakuza) hanged. Olivia's will kept the census logic alive after she died.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claimant is often real: test both before hanging or shooting either
tips_feedback.why: Frank and Grace both claimed Tracker and both were fake (Arsonist and Diviner). Trusting the duplicate gave cover to two non-Village players for days.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree covers on Night 1: a Village role fitting your tokens and visits
tips_feedback.why: Grace and Mallory had covers ready, but Bob held his claim back and then fitted Enforcer to Heidi's list, which made the whole town suspicious of him. The tip's advice to have a cover ready early would have saved him.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: list quiet unclaimed players and unexplained survivors
tips_feedback.why: Frank the Arsonist slipped through D2 on Innocent votes. On D4, his tracks always landing on non-visitors got him hanged for the Village win.

lessons.tip: Douse players likely to live, not the obvious Katana target. A douse on someone who dies to another cause is wasted. Day 1's agenda-setter or a freshly claimed investigator often dies that night, so douse quiet or confirmed-looking townies the Yakuza will leave alone.

Once you've survived a trial, ignite the next night, even with only 1-2 players doused. Each extra night of dousing gives a Fortune Teller or Cartographer another count with an unexplained visitor in it. Killing the player who is tracking the counts removes your biggest threat.

lessons.applies_to: Neutral killers / anyone with a fake visiting claim
lessons.tip: A Tracker cover whose every result is 'visited nobody' on passive-role players gets called uncheckable and wasted. Pick tracks that could be checked but probably won't be, or claim a role whose visits match your real douse targets. Then visit counts and Lookouts back up your story instead of leaving an unexplained extra visit.

At 4-5 alive, a 'Yakuza cleared' census or a Village-only trait (Armed, a Sniper shot) makes that player near-confirmed. If you attack them, the others will side with them. Get yourself out of the top suspect spot before the final few. Kill the counter or claimer before you're the only one left unexplained.

An alignment census counts only Good or Evil, never Neutral. So 'Evil 0' clears a player of Yakuza but not of being a Neutral killer. Use the census's Good count, or other checks, to rule out Neutrals.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once three players are doused, or two if you're being questioned; Arsonists who keep dousing usually hang first.
tips_feedback.why: The tip was right, and ignoring it cost me. I was questioned on Day 2 and kept dousing for two more nights. One douse was wasted on Erin, who died to the Katana, and another on Heidi, who was shot. I never ignited before I was hanged on Day 4.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claimant is often real: test both before hanging or shooting either.
tips_feedback.why: Grace and I both claimed Tracker, and the town accepted both. That plus the 1-in-3 holder argument got me acquitted 9-3 on Day 2. It bought me two nights, though in the end I was a fake claimant.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death and list quiet unclaimed players and unexplained survivors (a Not Evil read doesn't clear them).
tips_feedback.why: Niaj's Fortune Teller counts left one unexplained visitor on N1 and one on N3. Combined with my uncheckable tracks, that let the town find and hang me (the Neutral) at 4 alive.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action. A corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof; one unverified report is only that claimant's word.
tips_feedback.why: Town reasoning on Niaj's counts was what put me on trial twice. My douse visits kept showing up as extra visitors.

lessons.tip: With small Guilty totals, your vote can be worked out. If teammates are known to vote Guilty (for example a self-declared Zealot), joining them on a trial that fails 3-9 tells the town exactly who the third Guilty voter was. On trials that are going to fail anyway, vote with the town majority.

Never claim that you 'held' your action on a night your team killed. A blank night is exactly the gap a Katana holder needs in visit counts like the Fortune Teller's. Claim a concrete result that can't be checked, on a target whose visits fit the counts, and post it before anyone asks.

Before you send the Katana, list where a claimed Trapper or protector has probably put their ward. A Trapper who says the trap is on 'another player, not Bob or Judy' almost certainly protected the town's top confirmed investigator. Hit someone else, or use a role whose attack isn't a visit (a Ritualist guess) on that player.

Killing an investigator doesn't erase a result if their will names their target. A Seer whose will says 'my pair is Bob+Carol; if I die, look at Bob' convicts Bob just by dying. Before killing them, weigh whether the kill confirms the very suspicion you're trying to bury.

In the endgame, check every surviving claim against the Fortune Teller's visited and visitor counts night by night. Look for a player whose track always lands on someone who never visits, or who claims nothing on the night the holder needed to be unaccounted for. Those claims can't be checked, so they deserve the most suspicion.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree covers on Night 1: a Village role fitting your tokens and visits
tips_feedback.why: My Tracker cover (no tokens, one visit) held through four Days. When Frank also claimed Tracker, the town accepted that both could be real.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claimant is often real
tips_feedback.why: Because duplicates are allowed, town treated the Frank/Grace Tracker clash as a 1-in-3 rather than a lie. That saved me on Day 2.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result would narrow your team
tips_feedback.why: We killed Ivan to stop his Bob+Carol Seer pair. His will named the pair, so his death was read as proof against Bob, and Bob was hanged the next Day.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana, assume a protector... Fresh claimants are often guarded or trapped
tips_feedback.why: We ignored it and sent the Katana at Olivia, the obvious trap target. The trap went off, my visit was exposed, and Dave's report put me under Alice's Sniper shot.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate: vote Yes and Guilty and say so
tips_feedback.why: I voted Guilty on Mallory and Bob and stayed off the suspect list both Days. My one slip was a separate vote: Guilty on Frank alongside them.

lessons.tip: After you post the list, match every list role to a claimant. A list role that no living player claims (here Arsonist and Ritualist) almost always belongs to someone who claimed a role that isn't on the list. Name those claimants as the pool and keep pushing until someone owns each role. Don't settle for 'only half are real, so missing claims are fine.'

Once a Seer's 'different' pair has been settled by hanging the other member, the surviving member says publicly every Day that the pair is resolved and the hanged player's vote pattern backs it. If you don't, an Armed player or a Vigilante may still treat you as half of an open coin flip and shoot you.

Visitor and visited counts (Fortune Teller, Cartographer) only rule out people who visited nobody. A Katana holder can make the Katana visit and use their own action too, and a Neutral killer adds visits as well. Don't let a count argument clear a claimed visitor whose result can't be checked (for example 'tracked a passive role, it went nowhere').

A player whose every night result lands on someone who never visits (a Scout, a Fortune Teller, an Archivist) is giving results nobody can check. Treat that as a lead early, before it costs a Day. Here the Tracker who did this was the Arsonist.
When two players claim the same role, don't accept both because 'roles can repeat'. If neither claim can be checked and neither role is on a known-real list such as the Archivist's, test both.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote; a held-back result looks retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: My archive went public before Census Taker, Fortune Teller and Sniper were claimed. That confirmed Olivia's and Alice's claims later, and it set up a 12-0 hang of Mallory, who was the Ritualist.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claimant is often real: test both before hanging or shooting either.
tips_feedback.why: Frank and Grace both claimed Tracker and both were fakes (Arsonist and Diviner). Grace openly used 'Trackers can repeat' as cover, and the town never tested either of them.

tips_feedback.tip: A player who self-nominates or pushes with no data is often a Jester, who also reads Evil.
tips_feedback.why: Judy pushed Bob hard with no data and claimed late. She turned out to be the Executioner, and her revenge killed Olivia. The tip correctly flagged her as Neutral.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid hinting at a power role early or announcing tonight's target.
tips_feedback.why: I said only that I had info and posted it once there were claims to test. The Katana went to Erin and Ivan, not to me, so the hint didn't cost me.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows someone Yakuza, suspect whoever argued to delay their hang, defended them or PM'd them.
tips_feedback.why: Bob turned out to be Yakuza and had pushed the count onto Frank while holding back his own target. In the end Grace's lone Guilty on Frank (alongside Bob and Mallory) was what Alice used to justify her correct shot on Grace.

lessons.tip: Don't say publicly that you still have a chosen-pair token. It tells the Yakuza which check is coming and makes you the next Katana target. Spend it on the first night it can settle a live suspect, and say only 'I have a result' until you post it.

lessons.applies_to: Seer (and any checker with a pair or group check)
lessons.tip: Pair the suspect with a player who is already nearly confirmed Good, so SAME or DIFFERENT decides the suspect alone. Write the will to cover both outcomes ('if DIFFERENT, X is not Good'), because the result of the night you die never reaches your will. Even if you die that night, the will still sets the town's next hang.

Be suspicious of a claimed Tracker or Lookout whose every target is a player who never visits (a Scout, a passive Fortune Teller, a passive Archivist). 'They visited nobody' can't be checked, so it's the safest fake result. Two 'Trackers' with only uncheckable results are not shown real just because Trackers can repeat.

If someone pushes one player hard from the first day, with no data and no role claim, think of an Executioner. Hanging their target makes them win and sets up a Divine revenge on a random Guilty voter the next night. If that player is still the right hang, cap the Guilty votes at a bare majority, and keep confirmed investigators and Bonded players off the Guilty side.

Fortune Teller counts rarely single out one person. The Katana holder can visit two players (own action plus Katana), a Sleepwalker adds a random visit, and a Census 'Evil 0' still leaves Neutrals possible. List every assignment that fits the numbers before using the count to justify a hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid hinting at a power role early or announcing tonight's target: it usually draws the Katana, a block or a Ritualist guess.
tips_feedback.why: I broke this tip. I hinted 'I have something too' on Day 2, then claimed Seer with my token unused. The Yakuza named my spare token as their reason to kill me on Night 2. The tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it, so post what matters publicly.
tips_feedback.why: My will named the Bob+Carol pair and how to read either result. After I died, Judy and Dave built the Day 3 case on it, and Bob (Talent Agent) was hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claimant is often real: test both before hanging or shooting either.
tips_feedback.why: Grace used 'Trackers can repeat' to cover her fake Tracker claim next to Frank's. Both 'Trackers' were fake: Frank was the Arsonist and Grace was a Diviner. The tip helped keep both alive for days.

tips_feedback.tip: A player who self-nominates or pushes with no data is often a Jester, who also reads Evil.
tips_feedback.why: Judy (Executioner) fit this pattern by pushing Bob with no data. Bob was still the right hang, but 9 Guilty votes gave the revenge a wide pool. It killed Olivia (Census Taker), and Carol died with her through Bonded heartbreak.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result would narrow your team (Census Taker, Oracle, Accountant, visit counters)
tips_feedback.why: Helped the Yakuza: they killed me before I could post my Bob+Carol result. The will made up for it.

lessons.tip: Push your target in the town's own words: demand a plain claim, set a deadline ('if it's still missing on my next turn, I'll nominate'), and vote with the majority on everyone else. When your target holds back info, you look like a diligent villager, not a Neutral.

Pick an Astral, tokenless investigative cover (Juror, Oracle) and write a full fake result in your will early. It never shows up in Fortune Teller, Tracker or visit-group data, so nobody can mechanically break it, even if you only claim once you're under pressure.

A Census Taker's count never includes Neutrals. 'Evil 1 among X, Y and a known-Good' doesn't mean X or Y is the Yakuza when one of them could be Neutral. A Neutral in the group can steer the town at the other one. Check the unclaimed member's role before treating the census as a coin flip.

A hang that a quiet or late-claiming player pushed hard can be an Executioner's win. The revenge Divine Attack then lands on a random Guilty voter. If an Evil read is solid, keep Guilty votes near a bare majority so fewer villagers are exposed to Executioner or Jester revenge.

Killing an investigator doesn't stop their result if their will names tonight's target. Ivan's will named a Bob+Carol pair, and that alone condemned Bob. Kill the investigator the night before they commit to a target, or make sure the teammate in that check has an airtight cover.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote; a held-back result looks retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Bob held back his N1 target until Heidi's list and Grace's track were public. Then he claimed Enforcer on Heidi, and the whole table read it as retrofitted. That made it easy for me (Executioner on Bob) to push him.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it, so post what matters publicly.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan was Katana'd, but his will named his Bob+Carol pair, and that alone turned the town on Bob. Carol's will also confirmed her marks and her bond to Olivia.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result would narrow your team (Census Taker, Oracle, Accountant, visit counters); near parity, kill the Vigilante or Sniper instead.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza killed Ivan to stop his Bob check, but his will exposed the check anyway, and Olivia's census on Bob got through the same night. The kill telegraphed exactly whom they were protecting.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree covers on Night 1: a Village role fitting your tokens and visits, not a Yakuza-only role. Switching claims when cornered is usually fatal.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Enforcer cover matched his Disguise, but it claimed a visit that Talent Agent never makes. Once Chronicler marked him and he flipped Talent Agent, every N1 count was re-solved and his teammates were exposed.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately... a Not Evil read doesn't clear them.
tips_feedback.why: Nobody hunted the Arsonist (Frank) until the end, and he doused three people uncaught. In the final four, Niaj's push on Frank's unverifiable tracks found him, so the town won.

lessons.applies_to: Ritualist (and any Yakuza with one-shot kill tokens)
lessons.tip: Use the ritual guess on Night 1 if there is any reasonable read, for example a Day 1 agenda-setter as an investigator, or a teammate's Diviner read on a player. Yakuza often get hanged on Day 2 from random Seer pairs or counts, and unused tokens die with you. Holding them 'until a solid read' usually means never using them.

When an Archivist-style list names roles before anyone claims them, and later claims match it, the town will treat it as proven. Don't attack its credibility to save yourself, because that only makes you look worse. Choose a cover role that is plausibly among the list's fakes, and argue instead about who the other half of the pair could be.

Announce your forced vote trait at your first trial vote, before you're ever in danger. If you claim it for the first time during your own trial, it reads as a convenient excuse. An early claim also makes the totals match your words later.

Your random visit counts in Fortune Teller, Cartographer and Scout numbers, so claim a role that visits exactly one player a night (Lookout or Tracker). Then the visitor count fits your claim. Pick a target nobody else is likely to report on.

Killing an investigator whose will names the check they just made (for example 'Seer pair on Bob') points the town right at that teammate. If a check on a teammate is already locked in, consider killing someone else and preparing the teammate's cover for the result.

tips_feedback.tip: Tokens die with you, so spend one-shot tokens the first time they can matter.
tips_feedback.why: I didn't follow it. Following our team plan, I held both ritual tokens on N1 and was hanged on D2 with both still unused, so my kill role did nothing all game.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate: unless your votes can stop the hang, vote Yes and Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Bob and Grace voted Guilty on me 12-0 and didn't defend me. That kept them out of suspicion for a while, and Grace lasted until Day 4.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result would narrow your team (Census Taker, Oracle, Accountant, visit counters)
tips_feedback.why: Killing Ivan on N2 didn't stop his Bob+Carol pair, because his will posted it and said 'if I die, look at Bob'. Olivia's census also narrowed it to Bob or Judy, so the kill only confirmed the suspicion on Bob.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree covers on Night 1: a Village role fitting your tokens and visits
tips_feedback.why: My Lookout cover fit my Sleepwalker visit and Niaj's 7-visitor count exactly, so the count never broke it. I was caught by Ivan's random Seer pair, not by the cover.

lessons.applies_to: Fortune Teller / anyone using visit counts
lessons.tip: A count that matches the claims only shows the number of lies balances out, not that each claim is true. A Sleepwalker's hidden visit plus one invented target, or a holder making two visits, can still give the same totals. Before you act on a count, list every way it could fit.

Don't spend a one-shot kill on a chain of 'if X's claim is true, then Y is evil'. If Yakuza lie about visiting someone, that someone isn't evil. Take a lead and a sign that the target's own claim is real (an archive naming roles before anyone claimed them) as evidence for them, and fire only at a player whose own claim is broken.

In a Seer 'different' pair, the bad one is usually the player whose result can't be checked and who claimed only after being named. A player whose result has already been confirmed by later claims is usually the good one. Don't flip that read later on a teammate's theory.

A player who keeps tracking or watching people who never visit (passive claimers, a Scout) is giving results nobody can check. That's a classic cover for an Arsonist or a Yakuza. Also, an 'Evil 0' census doesn't clear Neutrals.

Someone who pushes one player hard from Day 2 and never claims a role may be an Executioner. When their target is hanged they leave, and a random Guilty voter dies that night. Keep Guilty votes at a bare majority, or keep your protected players' votes off that hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Tokens die with you... Kill shots need a real lead, not a claim clash or a 'test', but shouldn't wait for proof.
tips_feedback.why: I fired my hidden gun on N3 because of an inference chain, not a real lead, and killed Heidi, a Good Archivist. I took the 'shouldn't wait for proof' half too far.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, so a duplicate claimant is often real: test both before hanging or shooting either.
tips_feedback.why: Frank and Grace both claimed Tracker and both were fake (Arsonist and Diviner). The tip made people slower to doubt the double claim.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately... a Not Evil read doesn't clear them.
tips_feedback.why: Once the Yakuza were gone, Frank (an Arsonist) was the last threat. Hanging him on Day 4 won the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's will named his Bob+Carol pair. That pointed the town at Bob, and he was hanged and revealed as Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Survival confirms nothing: a Katana survivor with no named protector...
tips_feedback.why: The trap went off on N3 and no hitback death followed. That showed the attacker had Defense (Grace self-Divined), and it backed Alice's shot on Grace.

lessons.applies_to: everyone (especially Bonded players and key investigators)
lessons.tip: Before you vote Guilty on a hang that is already safe, think about Executioner and Jester revenge. If the nominee has been pushed hard by one player who has no checkable role, assume an Executioner may be targeting them. The revenge hits a random Guilty voter. When the Guilty total is well past the majority, a valuable or Bonded player can quietly vote Innocent to stay out of that pool. Votes are secret and only totals show.

A census never counts Neutrals. So when a group of three reads 'Evil 1' and one member is a dead Katana victim, the other two are not simply a 50/50 Yakuza split. One of them may be a Neutral who is framing the other. Say so publicly before the town hangs, and check whose push started the case.

lessons.applies_to: investigators who expect to be targeted
lessons.tip: Once you've publicly claimed and given useful results, expect the Katana and plan for your next result being lost. Post tonight's census target and the deductions each possible count would give (e.g. 'around Heidi: if Good 2 among Carol/Grace/Heidi, Grace is Yakuza') during the Day. Then even a will written before the result can still be read by town.

Don't put a suspicion in your will that a hang has already resolved. When one player of a Seer's 'different' pair is hanged, their earlier lies (such as a claimed Lookout visit that broke the visit count) strongly suggest they were the non-Good one. Pointing back at the other player of the pair just misleads town and can get a Good player shot.

Two players claiming the same no-token info role, with results that can never be checked (tracking players who never visit), make a strong lead. Ask each to track someone whose visits are known, and compare against the Fortune Teller's counts.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it, so post what matters publicly.
tips_feedback.why: My will held N1 and N2, which proved Bob and Judy after their flips. My N3 census (Carol/Grace/Heidi Good 2, which would have shown Grace was Yakuza) was lost because I died that night. That is exactly the gap this tip warns about.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote; a held-back result looks retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Posting my N1 census on Day 2 cleared Carol and Dave and broke the visit count. Posting N2 narrowed things to Bob or Judy, which led to Bob, a Yakuza Talent Agent, being hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: A player who self-nominates or pushes with no data is often a Jester, who also reads Evil. Prefer another hang, or keep Guilty votes to a bare majority.
tips_feedback.why: Judy pushed Bob from Day 2 with no data and was an Executioner targeting him. We hanged Bob 9-1 and Executioner revenge killed me (and Carol through heartbreak). Keeping Guilty votes to a bare majority would have cut that risk. I ignored the tip and it cost two Good players.

tips_feedback.tip: Survival confirms nothing: a Katana survivor with no named protector and a Not Evil read fits a Serial Killer.
tips_feedback.why: On Day 4 Frank used Dave's trap going off with nobody dying of the hitback to cast doubt on Dave. That survival was really Grace's self-Diviner Strong Defense, which shows how many explanations a survival can have.

summary:
The Village won. Two information roles decided the game. Carol (Chronicler) marked Erin on Night 1, so Erin was revealed as a Scout, a true anchor result. Carol then marked Bob on Night 2, which made hanging him safe: he was revealed as Talent Agent, a Yakuza role.

Olivia's Night 2 census of Bob, Ivan and Judy found 1 Evil. Together with Ivan's will, which named his chosen pair of Bob and Carol, that left the Village sure about Bob even though Ivan was killed before he could post the result.

On Day 2, Heidi's archive named Census Taker, Fortune Teller and Scout before anyone had claimed them. That made her credible, so Ivan's random Seer pair (Mallory and Heidi have different alignments) got Mallory hanged at 12–0. Mallory's late Zealot reveal and her "Heidi could be Neutral" argument changed no votes.

The Yakuza hurt themselves early. Bob held his claim back all day, then claimed Enforcer, a role from Heidi's list, with a "visit" to the one player whose visit data was already public. Nearly everyone named that as the weakest fit.

Judy (Executioner, target Bob) pushed Bob from Day 2 with no data, claimed Juror (Astral, so it can't be checked) only once Bob was on trial, and won when he was hanged. Her revenge killed Olivia, and Olivia's Bonded partner Carol died of heartbreak.

On Night 3, Grace used her Diviner action on herself for Strong Defense, which was clever. She survived the hitback from Dave's trap, and the same trap stopped her Katana attack on Olivia. Niaj then wasted his Armed shot on Heidi, a Good Archivist. He acted on Ivan's pair even though hanging Mallory had already explained it.

On Day 4, Alice used her Sniper shot well. Grace had publicly said Guilty on Frank and the total was exactly 3, so Grace was the only Guilty vote not explained by Bob and Mallory. Grace had also left a "held my track" gap on Night 2. Alice killed her with a Strong shot.

Frank, the Arsonist, doused three players but never ignited. All his Tracker results were "visited nobody" on players who never visit, and a nomination by Niaj got him hanged as the last bad player.

lessons.tip: Post your cover claim and night target early, before other players' data comes out. A claim that arrives just after someone posts a role list or visit data, and fits it neatly, looks retrofitted. Most players will name it as the least trustworthy fit.
lessons.evidence: Bob held back his role and target all Day 2 while five players asked for them. He then claimed Enforcer, a role on Heidi's list, with a visit to Heidi, the only player with public visit data. Heidi, Ivan, Judy, Niaj, Olivia, Alice and Carol all called it the weakest fit. That made him the main suspect even before Olivia's census and Carol's mark confirmed him.

lessons.tip: Fortune Teller and Cartographer counts show where claims break. Remember that the Katana holder can also use their own role's action, so a count only rules out players who claim no visit at all. Don't hang on a count that fits several holders.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 the 7 visitors / 4 visited count was first read as pointing only at Frank. Frank showed that Grace or Bob could fit too, Dave added the holder-also-acts point, and the Village wisely acquitted Frank 3–9. The count's real culprit was Bob's fake visit to Heidi.

lessons.applies_to: Village players with a one-shot kill (Armed, Vigilante, Sniper)
lessons.tip: Before shooting, check whether the suspicion has already been explained. A Seer 'different' pair is used up once its non-Good half has been hanged and confirmed by other evidence, and a Yakuza lying about visiting someone is no evidence against the person named.
lessons.evidence: Niaj shot Heidi on Night 3 because of Ivan's Mallory/Heidi pair and Bob's fake visit to her. Mallory had already been hanged as Yakuza, and Heidi's list had named unclaimed roles correctly. Niaj killed a Good Archivist and wasted the gun.

lessons.tip: Use stated votes against the announced totals to find the hidden partner of a Yakuza already exposed. Anyone who publicly voted with known Yakuza on a failed trial that the rest of town opposed is a strong lead.
lessons.evidence: Frank's trial on Day 2 ended 3 Guilty, and Bob, Grace and Mallory had each said Guilty. Once Bob and Mallory were confirmed Yakuza, Alice named Grace as the only Guilty vote left. She also pointed to Grace's 'held track' gap on Night 2, then sniped her with a Strong shot on Day 4. Grace was Yakuza.

lessons.tip: If you fake an investigative role, sometimes give results that can be checked. Tracking only players who never visit, so every result is 'visited nobody', becomes its own tell over several days.
lessons.evidence: Frank (Arsonist) 'tracked' Erin (Scout), Niaj (Fortune Teller) and Heidi (Archivist), and every result was 'visited nobody'. On Day 4 Niaj and Alice both named this pattern when they hanged him.

lessons.tip: Ignite while your doused targets are still alive. Dousing players the Katana or gunmen kill wastes nights, and an Arsonist who never ignites is usually hanged with nothing to show for it.
lessons.evidence: Frank doused Erin (killed that night), Niaj, and Heidi (shot that night). He never ignited, and at the end only Niaj was still doused when Frank was hanged at 4 players.

lessons.tip: Yakuza: if you expect a trap, give the holder Defense (a Diviner on itself, a Kitsune charm) so it survives the hitback. Trapper: put your trap on the claimed investigator most likely to be killed next. It arms one night later, so place it early.
lessons.evidence: Dave moved his trap to Olivia (Census Taker) on Night 2, and on Night 3 it stopped Grace's Katana. Grace had used her Diviner action on herself for Strong Defense, so the trap's Strong hitback failed and she survived.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret: keep a notepad of stated votes and announced totals.
tips_feedback.why: Alice matched the 3 Guilty votes on Frank to Bob, Mallory and Grace's stated votes, which singled out Grace as the remaining Yakuza for her Day 4 snipe.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it, so post what matters publicly.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's will named his Night 2 Seer pair (Bob and Carol) and said what each result would mean. He died before learning it, but his will plus Olivia's census was enough for the Village to hang Bob.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote; a held-back result looks retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi posted her full archive before most claims, so it named Census Taker, Fortune Teller and Scout ahead of time. That made her credible and got Mallory hanged. Bob's held-back claim was read as retrofitted, exactly as the tip warns.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate: unless your votes can stop the hang, vote Yes and Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Bob and Grace voted Yes and Guilty on Mallory, and Grace did the same on Bob. That kept Grace hidden until Day 4. Her only exposure came from a Guilty vote on Frank, a trial where she wasn't following this tip.

tips_feedback.tip: Tokens die with you, so spend one-shot tokens the first time they can matter. Kill shots need a real lead.
tips_feedback.why: Alice spent her Sniper tokens on a real lead and killed Grace (Yakuza). Niaj spent his Armed shot early on a lead that was already used up and killed a Good Archivist, which shows why the 'real lead' part matters.

issues.description: Bob was a Talent Agent with the Disguised trait (shown as Enforcer). Carol marked him on Night 2, and when he was hanged on Day 3 the reveal said 'Talent Agent'. The Chronicler's reveal is an exact-role check, and R19 says exact-role checks see a Disguised player's disguise, so it should have shown Enforcer. The game also handled the disguise inconsistently: Heidi's Night 1 Archivist result correctly showed Enforcer for Bob. The wrong reveal settled the game's central question and broke a plan the Yakuza had built on their reading of the rules.

The Chronicler text says a marked player's death 'reveals their true role to everyone (an exact-role check, R19)'. 'True role' conflicts with R19, which says exact-role checks see a disguise. This probably caused the wrong reveal of Bob. The text should say outright that a Disguised player's disguise is shown.

Because of the wrong reveal, players drew false conclusions. Heidi's and Carol's wills said the Enforcer on Heidi's list was a fake that Bob had borrowed, when it was really his disguise showing up in an exact-role check. Heidi went on to say that at least 3 claimants were lying.
Carol was told 'You were attacked tonight (heartbreak) and died.' Under the Bonded trait, heartbreak isn't an attack, so the message should not call it one.

At setup the program logged a tips_stale error: the tips file had been checked against an older version of the rules. All 13 players were still given it, so they may have read tips that no longer hold.

The moderator summaries contain internal notes (the Night 2 summary says 'The held tell() to Dave only described his own trap placement, so nothing needed resending'), and the Night 1 summary was printed twice. No player saw these, but they make the log harder to read.
Frank's Day 4 claim reads 'D2: Innocent on Mallory? no: Guilty on Mallory'. He corrected himself inside the claim text, which suggests the claim tool gives no clean way to fix a mistake.
